report: Thursday 19 November. A quiet day for us. The trader placed no orders, so there were no fills and no costs, apart from a custody fee of a fraction of a cent. The morning note explains why. Quotes were stale at the start, about 879 minutes old, so they showed yesterday's close. Brent fell to 89.51 dollars, well below our 98 dollar bar for an oil trade. Gold sat near a 14-month low, around 3730, under a hawkish Fed and a strong dollar. European markets fell for a third day, led by miners. Novartis gave new guidance out to 2031, but headlines read it both ways, so there was no pharma trade. We still hold one position: 6 Infineon shares bought at 50.90 euros. They closed at 49.35, a paper loss of about 9.27 euros. The stop is about 46.82, roughly 5 percent below today's price. The exit date is Tuesday 24 November, three trading days away. The account gained 0.84 euros today and stands at 1988.19 euros, down 0.59 percent overall. Reconcile is consistent, with no warnings and no rejected orders. The first shadow call has scored: BP up over 5 days was wrong, down 0.18 percent. One call and one quiet day show nothing about skill. Staying flat on unclear news is a choice, not proof of good judgment.
questions: The trader started with quotes about 879 minutes old, effectively yesterday's close. Should the rules forbid new entries until a fresh quote is available, or move the decision run later in the morning?

Infineon is about 3 percent below entry with a fixed exit on 24 November. Should the time-based exit stay strict, or may it be extended when the catalyst still stands, and how would we keep that from becoming an excuse to hold losers?

The BP shadow call was scored wrong on a move of only -0.18 percent, with confidence 0.47. Should shadow calls need a move larger than round-trip costs to count as right or wrong, and should calls under 0.5 confidence be recorded at all?
